answer: The draper marks the selvedge of every piece of cloth and enters the piece in his roll against the weaver who wove it. A echo piece bought from another draper fails the roll: at the fable of the selvedge the cloth must match the draper's own mark, and bought cloth shrinks in the wash. Forging a piece means hiring a draper, buying false cloth and paying 13,100, and the island line in the mark roll is kept by the guild, so cloth whose selvedge was never marked is cut up for rags.
